description: The Framework for Climate Adaptive Buildings is a method published by the Dutch Green Building Council to determine physical climate risks at the level of a single building, developed from 2022 with financial institutions, knowledge institutes, advisers and governments. The page read on 2026-09-28 (published 13 June 2024, edited 7 September 2026) describes three steps: an area score for exposure to heat stress, subsidence in drought, waterlogging and flooding, based on layers of the national climate impact atlas; a building score for vulnerability from building characteristics; and an adaptation strategy of area and building measures, with the two scores combined into a building climate risk score. Because some atlas layers were renamed, changed or withdrawn, DGBC now offers the original layers for download for use in GIS software such as QGIS. Coverage is the Netherlands. Access is free download; no licence is stated. Caveats: scores are indicator based and not calibrated against losses. It supports climate adaptation screening of building portfolios, such as ranking assets for EU Taxonomy reporting. No related building climate risk method record is catalogued.
